name: medium-core-off-reboot-secondary
title: MLAG secondary reboot · Medium lab, STP off on the MLAG pair, RSTP on the access switch (campus option 1)
action: Resets the data bridge on all three CHRs over management SSH: protocol-mode=none and forward-reserved-addresses=no on both MLAG peers, protocol-mode=rstp priority=0x0000 on the access switch, with edge=yes on its uplink bond and edge=yes, bpdu-guard=yes and loop-protect=on on its host port ether4, and reads the access switch port settings back. It requires a loss-free probe baseline, no BPDU from or through the MLAG pair and one copy of each broadcast. It then reboots CHR 2 (MLAG secondary, mlag-priority=20) with `/system reboot`, waits for the guest uptime to reset and keeps probing for 16 s plus a 3 s recovery window.

phases.name: Secondary down
phases.expected: CHR 1 (MLAG primary) keeps the shared system ID, so the access switch's uplink bond and traffic host 2 keep their LACP partner and forward over their members to CHR 1. The virtual links keep carrier, so they drop the member to CHR 2 only at the LACP short timeout (3 × 1 s). The access switch stays its own RSTP root and its edge uplink keeps forwarding, because a member leaving the bond does not change the bridge port.

phases.name: Secondary back
phases.expected: CHR 2 keeps its bond members out of the 802.3ad bond until the MLAG system ID syncs with CHR 1 (mlag-init-delay), then adds them under the unchanged shared system ID. The access switch re-adds the member to its uplink bond, which stays a forwarding edge port, so loss is brief or none.
